clue.text: Titled resident

parts.note: titled suggests a noble with a title, but here it means someone holding the title deeds to the home they live in

explanation.surface: A lord or lady living in some grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titled' pretends to mean aristocratic; in property terms it means holding legal title, so the resident owns the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds the deeds to a home and also lives there is described by this property term.

clue.text: Rapidly stirred drink left unfinished by journalist

indicators.note: the drink loses its last letter, so it is left without its ending

parts.note: whisky is a spirit drink
ED is the usual short form of editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter abandons a half-drunk glass of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating eggs or cream quickly with a whisk is a brisk kind of stirring.

clue.text: Greek deity has priestess decapitated initially

indicators.note: her name first loses its head letter before anything else happens

parts.note: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite in the legend of Hero and Leander
has can be shortened to 's, as in it's for it has

explanation.surface: A god of Greek myth comes with a beheaded priestess.
explanation.walkthrough: HERO without its first letter gives ERO; 's, a contraction of 'has', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love was son of Aphrodite, a deity of the pantheon.

clue.text: Book dedicated to all of the Romans?

definitions.text: Book dedicated to all of the Romans?

parts.words: Book dedicated to all of the Romans?
parts.note: the Latin word for for all names a collected volume, as if a Roman had dedicated the book to everyone

explanation.surface: A tome written for every citizen of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin dative plural meaning 'for all' is also the name for a book collecting several works.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected edition gathering several works in one volume takes its name from Latin meaning for all.

clue.text: Gold medallist removing head from house plant

indicators.note: removing says a letter is taken out of the medallist's title

parts.note: a gold medal winner is a champion

indicators.note: head from picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An Olympic winner leaves the top of a house and becomes a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The house's first letter, H, comes out of CHAMPION.
explanation.definitionFit: Red and white wild flowers of the pink family go by this name.

clue.text: There's some wine left

definitions.meaning: the left-hand side of a ship, the nautical term for left

explanation.surface: Somebody notices a little wine remaining in the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a fortified Portuguese wine and the sailor's word for the left side of a vessel.

clue.text: Position within peer group

parts.note: peer group suggests one's social equals, but read as the House of Lords it means raising someone to the peerage

explanation.surface: Finding one's place among friends of the same age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer group' sounds like sociology; read literally it is the body of peers, the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the rank of a lord is to place them among the nobility.

clue.text: Party activity focussed on dwindling number of seats?

definitions.text: Party activity focussed on dwindling number of seats?

parts.words: Party activity focussed on dwindling number of seats?
parts.note: sounds like a political party losing seats, but describes a children's party game where a seat is removed each round

explanation.surface: A political party worrying about losing seats in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'seats' suggest elections; the party is a birthday party and the seats are real chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: In this party game players circle seats while music plays and one seat is removed each round.

clue.text: Device for reducing scale?

parts.note: scale suggests a map or model size, but means the limescale deposits that hard water leaves

explanation.surface: A gadget that shrinks a map or model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' is the chalky deposit in kettles and pipes, which this appliance prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: This appliance removes calcium from hard tap water so less limescale builds up.

clue.text: Scottish supporter's run out clutching foreign coin

indicators.note: clutching says the first rearranged word holds the second inside it
out means the letters of the word run are thrown out of their order
foreign signals that the word coin is turned into something strange, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish fan gets run out while holding a coin from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' gives URN; 'foreign coin' gives NICO; URN 'clutching' NICO makes U-NICO-RN.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic beast holding up Scotland's royal coat of arms is one of its supporters.

clue.text: Girl's mother going about country with duke

indicators.note: going about says the mother's letters surround the others

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A girl's mother travels round a country with a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, borne by Prospero's daughter in The Tempest.

clue.text: Think you'll pot black

indicators.note: pot means to hold as a container does, so the phrase before it holds the letters

explanation.surface: A snooker player expects an opponent to sink the black ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, to 'pot' a ball is to sink it; here 'pot' says the preceding words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stained dark like ink is very dark in colour.

clue.text: Mean to pack old trains full to overflowing

indicators.note: to pack means the first word is filled with the second

parts.note: to mean to do something is to aim to do it
BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway

explanation.surface: Someone intends to cram old railway carriages until they overflow.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled up to the very edge, a brimming vessel is at bursting point.

clue.text: Stop old South African giving away rand

indicators.note: giving away says a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Someone tells an old South African to stop handing out money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command, but an organ stop is a set of pipes; several are named after instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ stop imitating a reed woodwind instrument carries this name.

clue.text: Leaf revealed when turning over topsoil often

indicators.note: turning over says the hidden letters are read backwards
revealed shows the letters lie visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A leaf appears whenever a gardener turns the topsoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'revealed when' in the definition; the definition is just 'Leaf', and 'revealed' marks the hidden word. OILOF read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sheet of a book, numbered on its front side only, is a leaf.

clue.text: Bitter cold in desert

indicators.note: in says the cold letter goes inside the desert word

parts.note: a desert is arid, utterly dry

explanation.surface: A biting chill in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sharp, pungent, unpleasant taste or smell.

clue.text: Couple taken in by a stratagem, endlessly difficult to accomplish

indicators.note: taken in by says the couple is placed inside the following pieces
endlessly means the last letter of the trick word is dropped

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem
a duo is a pair, a couple

explanation.surface: A pair fall for a cunning trick, which proves very hard to pull off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as deceived; here it puts DUO inside A + RUS (RUSE without its end).
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is laborious and strenuous is one hard to complete.

clue.text: Uncle's upset about Unionist centre

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the single letter
upset means the letters of the uncle word are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle is annoyed about a Unionist political hub.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLES rearranged gives NUCLES, which goes 'about' U.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of an atom or cell is its central part.

clue.text: Mineral, cold one imbibed by Scottish boy

indicators.note: imbibed by means the following letters are drunk up inside the boy's name

parts.note: Calum is a common Scottish boy's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad drinks a cold glass of mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: C and I go inside CALUM after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This metallic element, found in chalk and bones, is a dietary mineral.

clue.text: Her veal's cooked in port

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter here

explanation.surface: A woman's veal dish is prepared in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Seine estuary is a major French seaport.

clue.text: Rifle contents of gallery, to be loaded into car

indicators.note: to be loaded into says the art goes inside the car word

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
a gallery contains art

explanation.surface: Someone raids a gallery and loads the paintings into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a verb, to ransack; it is the noun, the Martini-Henry rifle of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Martini-Henry was a breech-loading British army rifle of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Soap fragment?

parts.note: suggests a sliver broken off a bar of soap, but means a series derived from a television soap opera

explanation.surface: A small piece broken off a bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' is a soap opera; a series developed out of it is described by this term.
explanation.definitionFit: A new show developed from characters in an existing series is derived from it.

clue.text: Bombastic broadcast on Wells

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A pompous radio programme about the city of Wells, or about H G Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' recalls Orson Welles's radio show; it scatters the seven letters of ON WELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated or puffed-up language is described as turgid or pompous.

clue.text: Sign about classical art gets people involved in a row

indicators.note: about says the sign word goes round the next piece

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come
ars is the Latin, or classical, word for art

explanation.surface: An omen about ancient art leads people into an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers who pull the oars of a boat take part in rowing.

clue.text: Long account given by ambassador

parts.note: HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador delivers a lengthy report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or pine for something is to long for it.

clue.text: Staff exposing criminal

definitions.meaning: a shepherd's or bishop's hooked staff

explanation.surface: An employee is revealed as a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a hooked shepherd's stick and a swindler or thief.

clue.text: Accurate translation European Union rejected

parts.note: TR is the abbreviation for translation

indicators.note: rejected means the union's letters are sent back the other way

explanation.surface: A precise translation is turned down by the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Something correct or exact is faithful to the facts.

clue.text: New poem makes a significant point

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A fresh poem makes an important argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction or key point in a network or graph is an important point.

clue.text: Ken's having a month off for examination

indicators.note: off says the month is taken away from the word before

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was London's first elected mayor, so something of his is mayoral
May is a month of the year

explanation.surface: Ken takes a month's leave before a test.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London from 2000 to 2008, so 'Ken's' gives MAYORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as opposed to a written paper, is a type of exam.

clue.text: Instrument used in attack almost as a matter of course

indicators.note: used in says the instrument goes inside the attack word
almost means the attack word loses its final letter

parts.note: a raid is an attack
a viol is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is routinely used as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a matter of course' reads as 'routinely'; the definition is 'a matter of course', a dish served as one course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed pasta parcels are served as a dish, one course of a meal.

clue.text: Story about Arab, by American in wild west town

indicators.note: about says the story word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A tale about an Arab and an American in a frontier town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Wyoming city grew from a frontier fort of the old American West.

clue.text: Unrestrainedly drinking in the ambience of the Piazza San Marco?

definitions.text: Unrestrainedly drinking in the ambience of the Piazza San Marco?

parts.words: Unrestrainedly drinking in the ambience of the Piazza San Marco?
parts.note: describes someone getting blind drunk in Venice, but names a window shade with slats

explanation.surface: A tourist drinking heavily in St Mark's Square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' is slang for very drunk; the Piazza San Marco is in Venice; together the phrase names a slatted window blind.
explanation.definitionFit: A window covering of horizontal adjustable slats goes by this Italian-city name.
